observations.seen: Frame 1 has a blue spotlight hotspot burned into the court centre. Frame 2 (moon) lights only the court and leaves the surround nearly black. Frames 3 and 4 use one warm directional key with weak fill, so the stands read flat.

Players and stands cast directional shadows that are hard-edged and long in frames 2 to 4. Frame 1 shows soft contact shadows under the players. Neither style shows ambient occlusion where the stands meet the floor.
No surface shows specular response or environment reflection. The net posts, umpire chair and court surfaces are all fully matte.

The stands are boxes on a large empty floor plane that fills about a third of each frame. The venues differ through a moon sphere and blurred tower or scaffold backdrops, but the floor itself has no detail.
The only haze is whitish fog in the corners of frame 1. Frames 2 to 4 show no indoor haze or light shafts from the floodlight poles, which the indoor-haze recipe calls for.

Surfaces are flat-shaded solid colours. The exceptions are a procedural noise texture on the frame 1 hard court and mow stripes on the frame 4 grass. The clay has no grain or scuffing, and the lines show no wear.

Spectators are repeated capsule or voxel figures in random colours. Players are low-poly with simple heads. The bench and umpire chair are plain boxes, and the player in frame 2 clips through the AURA SLAM sign text.

The court fills roughly 35 to 40% of the frame, which matches the 25 to 40% target. The large untextured floor at the bottom and sides dilutes the framing, and the yellow target box draws more attention than the ball.

The elevated broadcast angle and narrow FOV stay consistent across frames 2 to 4, close to the 70° / FOV 40 recipe. Frame 1 is steeper and nearly top-down, and none of the frames use an orthographic projection.
No bloom on the floodlights or white lines and no visible colour grading. Only the backdrop is depth-blurred. The frame 1 vignette haze looks like a lighting artifact more than a deliberate grade.
